data.title: DOJ considers joining Texas BlackRock, State Street anitrust case - report
data.description:
The U.S. Department of Justice is evaluating joining a state-led antitrust lawsuit against BlackRock (BLK) and State Street (STT) concerning claims that the fund managers used their power to pressure coal producers to cut output. 

Senior DOJ officials have discussed the possibility of joining the lawsuits with the states recently, according to a  Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. No final decisions have been made and the regulator may decide not to do anything.

In November 2024, Texas and 10 other Republican state attorneys general sued BlackRock (BLK) and State Street (STT), claiming that the money managers pressured coal producers to cut output causing residents to pay higher power bills.

Vanguard Group, which was originally named as a defendant in the suit, settled this February, agreeing to pay $29.5 million and to stop imposing ESG goals for its investments. 

The DOJ declined to comment on if it will join the lawsuit, but told Bloomberg it's focused on “affordability for all Americans across our economy.” The Texas attorney general’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment. BlackRock declined to comment and referred to an earlier statement calling the suit "baseless."  State Street also declined to comment and said the "lawsuit remains baseless and without merit.”

data.title: Trump announces White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
data.description:
US President Donald Trump said he was banning CNN (WBD), MS NOW (VSNT) and Politico from the White House, accusing outlets of repeatedly publishing what he called “FAKE NEWS” about his administration and the country.

In a Friday Truth Social post, Trump said the ban was effective immediately and suggested other media organizations could face similar action.

Trump also criticized Politico over what he described as an $8 million subscription from the US government under former President Joe Biden, calling the payment “illegal and ridiculous” and saying it appeared to him to be corruption.

“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” Trump wrote.

He did not provide further details in the post about how the ban would be implemented or what specific reports from the three outlets prompted the action.

Trump referred to MS NOW (VSNT) as having recently changed its name from MSNBC, saying the change followed a lack of viewership and credibility. He concluded by saying other media outlets he considers “Fake News Media Outlets” could be targeted next.

The post did not provide additional information about the scope of the restrictions or how they would affect the outlets’ coverage of the White House.

data.title: Heir-apparent to TPG CEO leaves as boss stays put
data.description:
Todd Sisitsky, president of TPG (TPG), abruptly left the alternative asset manager earlier this month after 23 years at the firm, apparently frustrated by CEO Jon Winkelried's decision to retain the company's reins, according to a media report on Friday.

The heir apparent to the 66-year-old Winkelried had wearied of waiting for a chance to take over, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. A few days after Sisitsky left TPG, Wall Street rival CVC Capital Partners announced that he would become its co-CEO, along with CVC President Peter Rutland, by Q1 2028 as Rob Lucas steps back from the CEO role.

Winkelried has good reason to hold on. He stands to reap almost $500M in bonus compensation if he stays and the stock rebounds, the article said. 

TPG hasn't yet told key backers who will replace Sisitsky or how the firm will revamp its succession plan, the people told Bloomberg.

Winkelried, in late 2023, received a long-term award that vests in phases through January 2029. Based on goals already achieved, he would get shares currently valued at ~$260M. If the stock climbs to $70 by 2030 (it's currently at ~$46.50), he could get more than $450M, according to the company's filings. Earlier this year, he received a $25M retention award  that fully vests in 2031.

Winkelried joined TPG in 2015 as co-CEO then became sole CEO in 2021. In the past five years, TPG's stock has risen 35%, lagging the S&P 500's 72% increase during that same period.

The SA Quant system rates the stock as a Hold, while the average Wall Street rating is Buy.

data.title: SpaceX wins $946M NASA deal to extend ISS crew flights through 2030
data.description:
NASA on Friday said it has awarded SpaceX (SPCX) a $946 million contract for three additional astronaut missions to the International Space Station, extending the company’s crewed flights to the orbiting laboratory through 2030.

The award brings SpaceX’s (SPCX) total NASA astronaut missions under the contract to 17 and raises its total value to $5.92 billion. The agency is relying heavily on SpaceX (SPCX) to maintain regular crew transportation to and from the station while seeking to preserve Boeing (BA) as a second US option.

The contract covers astronaut and spacecraft preparations, launches, in-space mission operations, crew returns and capsule recovery. It also includes transporting supplies and keeping the spacecraft at the station as an emergency escape vehicle.

NASA selected SpaceX (SPCX) and Boeing (BA) in 2014 to develop spacecraft capable of carrying astronauts to the station, seeking to establish a regular US crew-launch capability after the retirement of the space shuttle ended years of reliance on Russia’s Soyuz spacecraft.

SpaceX’s (SPCX) role has grown after Boeing’s (BA) Starliner encountered problems during its 2024 crewed test flight. NASA returned the capsule without its crew, while astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams returned to Earth aboard SpaceX’s (SPCX) Crew Dragon after their planned 10-day mission stretched beyond nine months.

NASA approved SpaceX’s (SPCX) system for crewed flights in November 2020. Since then, SpaceX (SPCX) has become the agency’s main provider for rotating ISS crews, using Crew Dragon and Falcon 9 to carry as many as four astronauts and supplies.

NASA said it wants both companies operating crew flights so a technical problem or accident involving one provider does not interrupt US access to the station.

data.title: Lilly wins full FDA approval for Inluriyo combo in breast cancer
data.description:
Eli Lilly (LLY) on Friday announced that the U.S. FDA granted full approval for an all-oral regimen containing its estrogen receptor antagonist Inluriyo and kinase inhibitor Verzenio as a late-line option for breast cancer.

Specifically, the approval clears the combo for adults with estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer with an ESR1 mutation whose disease has progressed following one or more lines of prior endocrine therapy. The treatment is indicated for those with locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

The decision is based on data from the company’s Phase 3 EMBER-3 trial in which patients with ESR1-mutated MBC receiving Inluriyo with Verzenio as a late-line therapy doubled median progression-free survival compared to those who received Inluriyo alone.

Inluriyo belongs to a novel drug class known as oral selective estrogen receptor degraders. Roche’s (RHHBY) oral SERD giredestrant is currently under FDA priority review for ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, with a decision expected by Nov. 30.
